mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined in three of the last four weeks (-63.7 to -66.1), reflecting persistent erosion of non-essential outings. Absent a reversal signal elsewhere in the snapshot, this momentum is expected to continue, producing a further decline in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -63.7 to -66.1 over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is higher than the trailing-28-day mean (direction flips to +), the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility dropped sharply from -40.1 to -52.1 over the last two weeks, indicating a behavioral retreat from outdoor substitute activities. This retreat typically co-occurs with broader caution toward non-essential outings, predicting a continued decline in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 10 points over two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks despite the observed PARKS decline exceeding the threshold, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained elevated RESIDENTIAL (above 17 for four straight weeks) combined with still-suppressed WORKPLACES (around -50) signals an active stay-at-home policy regime. Under this regime, RETAIL_REC is expected to remain suppressed or decline further over the next four weeks as policy constraints persist.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 15 and WORKPLACES remains below -40 for the full snapshot window
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 17.1 and 18.0 across all four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks while RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES remain in the stated restrictive ranges, the regime-driven suppression hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility improved from -55.0 to -50.1 while TRANSIT remained flat near -60, suggesting a shift toward private-vehicle commuting rather than public transit use. This joint pattern of workplace recovery without transit recovery implies increased localized errand and retail activity near workplaces, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -55.0 (t-2w) to -50.1 (t-0w) while TRANSIT stayed near -60 to -62
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next four weeks despite continued WORKPLACES improvement and flat TRANSIT, or if WORKPLACES reverses its improving trend, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The snapshot falls in mid-January, immediately after the holiday mobility trough typically seen in retail categories. A short-term mean reversion toward pre-holiday routine shopping levels is expected, producing a modest rise in RETAIL_REC over the next week even without changes in restriction policy.
evidence_refs: fact:snapshot date is 2021-01-15, within the post-holiday normalization window
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline in the next week rather than rebounding toward pre-holiday levels, the seasonal reversion hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility falls below -65 week-on-week, indicating a sudden sharp reduction consistent with new restriction announcements or public caution, RETAIL_REC is expected to drop sharply the following week as the same behavioral caution extends to retail outings.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has fluctuated between -59.7 and -62.6 without yet breaching -65
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses below -65 but RETAIL_REC does not decline in the subsequent week, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The joint persistence of high RESIDENTIAL (>17), stalled WORKPLACES recovery, and flat TRANSIT together indicate a plateaued restriction regime rather than active reopening or tightening. Under this stable-but-restrictive joint condition, RETAIL_REC is expected to remain near its current suppressed level or decline slightly over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 17, WORKPLACES stays within -55 to -50, and TRANSIT stays within -63 to -59 simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:all three series show narrow week-to-week ranges over the snapshot period
failure_condition: If any one of the three series breaks out of its stated range and RETAIL_REC rises in response, the joint-plateau mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In winter, declining PARKS mobility (from -43.3 to -52.1) alongside stable elevated RESIDENTIAL reflects a seasonal shift away from outdoor substitute activities toward indoor confinement. Active during winter lockdown conditions, this pattern is expected to continue suppressing overall non-essential mobility, including RETAIL_REC, through the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined steadily while RESIDENTIAL stayed elevated across all four weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS stabilizes or rises while RETAIL_REC still declines, or if RETAIL_REC rises despite continued PARKS decline and stable high RESIDENTIAL, the seasonal-confinement hypothesis is rejected.
